description: The guard-apply approval envelope: what the Master signs, what the peer verifies, and how the two exchange it. The narrative contract is guard-protocol.md; this file is the machine-readable statement of the same rules, so a drift between the two implementations of the rule fails the contract test instead of failing a peer at 3am.

approval.empty_allowed_note: `content_b64` may be empty because an empty file is a legitimate target. `operator_os` may be empty because an approval can carry no attestation of the human behind it — and empty then means *unattested*, which the guard must refuse a privileged mutation for rather than read as permission. Present-but-empty is a value, not an omission: the field is inside the projection either way, so an approval cannot be silently stripped of it without breaking the signature.

operator_os.shape_when_present: the encoded form of contracts/identity-schema.json grant.fields.operator_os — uid, euid, username, groups, is_root
operator_os.why_a_string: guard_approval_message requires every projected field to be a string, so the attestation rides encoded rather than nested. Relaxing that rule was considered and rejected: a nested object would need its own canonicalisation, and the all-strings rule exists so no caller has to supply one.
operator_os.encoding: shared/sparknet-authz.py::encode_operator_os — canonical JSON (sort_keys, tight separators, ASCII), which is why two orderings of one attestation cannot produce two signatures
operator_os.decoding: shared/sparknet-authz.py::decode_operator_os — strict; a malformed encoding is refused rather than read as unattested, so a lost root attestation stays distinguishable in an audit from one that was never made
operator_os.enforced_by: shared/sparknet-authz.py::guard_approval_operator_allows, at the peer guard's apply path
operator_os.authority: The attestation authorises. Operator decision 2026-10-24: a minter is trusted, so an attested is_root:true permits a privileged mutation even when the serving daemon runs as somebody else. It complements the guard's euid_0 requirement rather than replacing it — the attestation says whether the human may ask, the uid says whether the process can do, and both must hold.

approval.signature_covers: the whole envelope, and nothing outside it

field_semantics.peer_fingerprint: sha256 of the target peer's canonical identity (contracts/identity-schema.json). Binds the approval to one peer: an approval minted for peer A is refused by peer B.
field_semantics.file_path: the protected path on the peer. The peer's own manifests/critical-manifest.json decides what is protected; the Master cannot widen it.
field_semantics.content_b64: the new file content, base64, inside the signature. Signing a digest alone would let anything on the path substitute the bytes.
field_semantics.content_sha256: sha256 hex of the new content. The peer recomputes it and refuses a mismatch.
field_semantics.issued_at: ISO-8601 UTC, when the Master minted the approval.
field_semantics.expires_at: ISO-8601 UTC, when the approval stops being valid. The peer's security policy bounds the window (manifests/security-policies.json).
field_semantics.nonce: single-use. The peer refuses a replayed nonce/request_id pair, and the Master refuses to issue the same nonce twice.

capability_source.where: the peer's own signed registry entry (manifests/node-authorizations.json)
capability_source.why_not_the_payload: The envelope carries no capabilities. A peer that read 'guard-apply' out of the payload would let an approval grant the very authority it is supposed to be checked against. The Master grants guard-apply once, in the registry; an approval only ever exercises it.

transport.payload_encoding: base64 of the canonical approval bytes
transport.signature_encoding: base64 of the Ed25519 signature over those canonical bytes
transport.source_gate: the peer accepts loopback and the Master's overlay address (10.100.0.1); every other source is refused with 403 off_overlay before the body is read
transport.peer_binding: the peer refuses an approval whose peer_fingerprint is not its own
